sentences.en: Um, so I have spent the last couple weeks, I guess, however long this started, um, talking to people who are concerned about really bad things happening around the election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我过去几周吧，或者说从这件事开始到现在，一直在和那些担心选举前后会发生非常糟糕的事情的人交谈。

sentences.en: Uh, so a couple of weeks ago, Andy and I called up our colleague Reed Epstein on the politics desk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以几周前，我和安迪给政治新闻组的同事里德·爱泼斯坦打了个电话。

sentences.en: We'd been hearing about concerns swirling around the possibility of violence around this year's presidential election.
sentences.zh: 我们一直听到人们对今年总统大选期间可能发生暴力的担忧。

sentences.en: And we were all trying to better understand what that was about.
sentences.zh: 我们都试图更好地了解这到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: You know, I talked to academics and people at think tanks and corporate security consultants.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我采访了学者、智库人员和企业安全顾问。

sentences.en: So Reed had gotten on the phone with all sorts of different professionals.
sentences.zh: 所以里德和各种各样的专业人士通过电话。

sentences.en: People who are in charge of keeping polling places safe and maintaining security at facilities where they're actually going to count the balance.
sentences.zh: 那些负责保障投票站安全以及维护实际点票场所安全的人员。

sentences.en: To sort of check the pulse of all these different people.
sentences.zh: 以此来摸清所有这些不同人群的脉搏。

sentences.en: People who monitor domestic extremist groups, uh, former State Department and Homeland Security officials.
sentences.zh: 监测国内极端主义团体的成员，嗯，前国务院和国土安全部官员。

sentences.en: Whose job it is to think about stuff like this.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作就是思考类似的事情。

sentences.en: And that they're taking extra from years before.
sentences.zh: 而且他们比往年采取了更多措施。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There certainly is, is more emphasis on security.
sentences.zh: 对安全的重视确实增加了。

sentences.en: Uh, a lot of people were very concerned that if there is not a decisive result on election day or the day after election day, and there's
sentences.zh: 嗯，很多人非常担心，如果在选举日或选举日过后的那几天没有得出明确的结果，并且

sentences.en: weeks of uncertainty that follows, that there could be a problem.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是数周的不确定性，那可能会出问题。

sentences.en: Or that the losing side mounts some sort of major protest event.
sentences.zh: 或者失败的一方会组织某种大型抗议活动。

sentences.en: There is a concern that something violent could happen.
sentences.zh: 人们担心可能会发生暴力事件。

sentences.en: Uh, and a lot of these people that I talked to are either making contingency plans or urging others to make contingency plans to be prepared in case things go haywire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我采访的很多人要么在制定应急计划，要么敦促其他人制定应急计划，以便在情况失控时做好准备。

sentences.en: And then there was this other thing Reid had been hearing about.

sentences.en: Something much more tangible.

sentences.en: You know, it's not uncommon for gun sales to go up before a presidential election.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在总统大选前枪支销量上升并不罕见。

sentences.en: And an incredibly diverse group of people.

sentences.zh: 有些人不是第一次买枪，但在此时此刻对枪支有了截然不同的看法。

sentences.en: I've owned guns for years, but I just recently for the first time purchased an AR rifle, partly because of what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我拥有枪支多年，但最近我生平第一次购买了一支 AR 步枪，部分原因就是因为现在发生的这一切。

sentences.en: But I came to Seattle to hear from people who were out buying guns specifically because they were worried about the possibility of violence from the political left.
sentences.zh: 但我来到西雅图是为了听取那些专门因为担心来自政治左翼的暴力可能性而出来买枪的人的意见。

sentences.en: I think the left, while they talk a lot about freedom and rights and this and that, I think they're more oppressive.
sentences.zh: 我认为左翼虽然口口声声谈论自由、权利这个那个，但我认为他们更具压迫性。

sentences.en: I think they're more closed minded.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们思想更加封闭。

sentences.en: The left claims that the right is intolerant and the right would say the left is becoming intolerant.
sentences.zh: 左翼声称右翼不宽容，而右翼则会说左翼变得不宽容了。

sentences.en: You know, if you have an opposing opinion, then you're somehow racially motivated or you're a right wing wacko.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你有反对意见，那你就是出于某种种族动机或者你是个右翼疯子。

sentences.zh: 骚乱和城市骚乱。

sentences.en: If that starts spreading out into the suburbs, I want to be in a position to defend myself and my home and my family.
sentences.zh: 如果这开始蔓延到郊区，我想处于能够保卫自己、我的家和我的家人的位置。

sentences.en: Here in the Seattle area, a lot of people pointed to what had happened in the region over the summer.
sentences.zh: 在西雅图地区，很多人都提到了今年夏天该地区发生的事情。

sentences.en: You have a lot of suburbanite people that have seen looting, assaults, you know, stopping of people's cars, damage, I mean, burning up of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你有很多郊区居民看到了打砸抢、袭击，你知道的，拦车、破坏，我是说，焚烧东西。

sentences.en: Where protests turned into riots and the Seattle City Council moved to defund their police department.
sentences.zh: 抗议活动演变成骚乱，西雅图市议会采取行动削减了警察局的经费。

sentences.en: They're there to create anarchy.

sentences.en: You know, this isn't a bunch of hippies smoking dope and listening to music at Woodstock.

sentences.en: They'll make your life miserable to get their way.
sentences.zh: 他们会让你生不如死，直到达到他们的目的。

sentences.en: And that's escalated to the point where it might not just be somebody judging you, but it might be something where you need to defend yourself.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经升级到这种地步：可能不仅仅是别人在对你评头论足，而是你可能需要开始保护自己了。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: Like, if I go to the grocery store, you know, I'm not going to have somebody rip me out of the car or put a gun at my face.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我去杂货店，你知道的，我不至于遇到有人把我从车里拉出来或者拿枪指着我的脸。

sentences.en: And you've gotten to the point where you're nervous that there are fractions of the left that would do something like that.
sentences.zh: 而现在事情发展到让你开始担心左翼中真的会有人做出这种事。

sentences.en: I would say so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我会这么说，是的。

sentences.en: Once you say it's okay to punch a Nazi and then you paint the other guy as a Nazi, you know, then boom, it's okay to kill a Nazi.
sentences.zh: 一旦你觉得殴打纳粹是合理的，然后又把其他人抹黑成纳粹，你知道的，那么轰的一下，杀掉纳粹也就变成合理的了。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And then you're a hero.
sentences.zh: 然后你就成了英雄。

sentences.en: You know, I don't want it to happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我可不想这种事发生。

sentences.en: Hopefully they don't have the guts.
sentences.zh: 但愿他们没那个胆子。

sentences.en: You know, hopefully they're all living in mom's basement, you know, but you just don't know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，但愿他们都还寄生在妈妈的地下室里，你知道的，但你永远说不准。

sentences.en: I think that they are pushing for a contested election so that they can ferment a civil war.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们正在极力推动一场有争议的选举，以便煽动内战。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't ever want to shoot anybody, man.
sentences.zh: 我从来不想向任何人开枪，老兄。

sentences.en: But, you know, to protect myself and my mom and my dog, man, you know, I guess if someone was trying to get in and harm us, I would.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，为了保护我自己、我妈和我的狗，老兄，你知道的，我想如果有人试图闯进来伤害我们，我会开枪的。

sentences.en: Hey, hello.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好。

sentences.en: Come on in.
sentences.zh: 请进。

sentences.en: I'll put on my mask, too.
sentences.zh: 我也把口罩戴上吧。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for doing this.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你接受采访。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，不客气。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, it's a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 不用谢，这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: One of those anxious people that I met in one of those lines actually let me go over to his place.
sentences.zh: 我在那些排队的人当中遇到过一个焦虑的人，他后来其实让我去他家里坐坐。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, so where do you keep the gun?
sentences.zh: 那么，那么你把枪放在哪里？

sentences.en: So I keep the gun in the safe.
sentences.zh: 枪我放在保险箱里。

sentences.en: It's by our bed.
sentences.zh: 就在我们床边。

sentences.en: To explain a little bit more about what it was that brought him out to the gun store.
sentences.zh: 为了进一步解释是什么促使他来到这家枪店。

sentences.en: It's a quick combination and I timed it and I can basically take it out, load it and theoretically aim it in 10 seconds so far.
sentences.zh: 只需输入一个简单的密码组合，我掐过时间，我基本上可以在10秒内把它拿出来、装好子弹，理论上还能瞄准。

sentences.en: Gotten a few practices in?
sentences.zh: 练习过好几次了吧？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 练过。

sentences.en: I got a security consultant to come here and he's also, you know, one of the trainers at the range.
sentences.zh: 我请了一位安全顾问来这里，他同时也是，你知道的，射击场的教练之一。

sentences.en: And so, you know, he was like, practice.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他当时说，要多练习。

sentences.en: He's like, even five minutes a day will really add up.
sentences.zh: 他说，哪怕一天练五分钟，日积月累下来效果也很显著。

sentences.en: So this is one of the things I practiced.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是我练习的内容之一。

sentences.en: What kind of gun is it?
sentences.zh: 这是什么类型的枪？

sentences.en: So it's an AR-15.
sentences.zh: 这是一把AR-15。

sentences.en: And this one is sort of, I would say, sort of like a middle of the road price point.
sentences.zh: 这把枪的价格，我可以说，算是比较适中的价位。

sentences.en: The dealer talked about how, you know, if you, if you spend extra, it will last longer.
sentences.zh: 枪械经销商说过，你知道的，如果你，如果你多花点钱，它就会更耐用。

sentences.en: And sort of in the mood that I bought, I didn't feel like cost was an object.
sentences.zh: 而且鉴于我当时的心境，我觉得价格并不是问题。

sentences.en: It's got your classic iron sights and your optics.
sentences.zh: 它配有经典的机械瞄具和光学瞄准镜。

sentences.en: He had just purchased an AR-15, a semi-automatic rifle, what the NRA actually calls America's most popular rifle.
sentences.zh: 他刚买了一把AR-15半自动步枪，也就是美国全国步枪协会（NRA）所称的美国最受欢迎的步枪。

sentences.en: There's a, the bolt action is supposedly more durable.
sentences.zh: 有一种，旋转后拉式枪机据说更耐用。

sentences.en: I'm definitely the wrong person to ask about these things though.
sentences.zh: 不过，向我打听这些事情我可真是一问三不知。

sentences.en: You're still learning.
sentences.zh: 你还在学习阶段。

sentences.en: I am very much, very much.
sentences.zh: 是的，还在学，一直在学。

sentences.en: Can you load the gun and show me how it works?
sentences.zh: 你能给枪装上子弹并向我展示它是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: So, you know, the standard procedure is that you've got the gun in the ready position, which can be either angled slightly upward or slightly downward.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，标准程序是把枪放在预备姿势，枪口可以微微朝上，也可以微微朝下。

sentences.en: We want upward for loading the gun.
sentences.zh: 装填子弹时我们要枪口朝上。

sentences.en: And so I pull back the charging handle, lock it back in.
sentences.zh: 然后我拉动拉机柄，将其向后锁定到位。

sentences.en: And so now we're just going to take out the clip.
sentences.zh: 现在我们要取出弹匣。

sentences.en: We're going to insert it, tug to make sure it actually stayed in.
sentences.zh: 将其插入，用力拉一下以确保它真的卡稳了。

sentences.en: And now press that.
sentences.zh: 现在按下那个按钮。

sentences.en: A live round is in the chamber.
sentences.zh: 一颗实弹已经上膛。

sentences.en: Safety's still on.
sentences.zh: 保险仍开着。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's pretty quick.
sentences.zh: 动作挺快。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It shows that you've been practicing.
sentences.zh: 看得出来你练过。

sentences.en: Well, my instructor will be pleased.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的教练听了会很高兴的。

sentences.en: I've enjoyed learning about it.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢了解这些的。

sentences.en: Let me help you pick up these bullets.
sentences.zh: 我来帮你把这些子弹捡起来吧。

sentences.en: He put his gun back into its safe.
sentences.zh: 他把枪放回了保险箱。

sentences.en: Before we move on, I know that you wanted to keep some things private, but what would you be comfortable?
sentences.zh: 在我们继续之前，我知道有些事情你想保密，但你愿意分享到什么程度？

sentences.en: Tell me about, um, with your education and your, your professional life.
sentences.zh: 能跟我聊聊，嗯，关于你的教育背景和你的职业生活吗？

sentences.en: I, I thought about this, uh, because I didn't want to identify myself too much.
sentences.zh: 我，我考虑过这个，呃，因为我不想暴露太多个人信息。

sentences.en: Um, and we walked over to his living room.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后我们走进了他的客厅。

sentences.en: I currently, I will say this, I work in tech, you know, that doesn't narrow it down much in Seattle.
sentences.zh: 目前，我只能透露这些：我在科技行业工作，你知道的，在西雅图这可划定不出什么具体范围。

sentences.en: Um, but I think that sort of being identified as having sort of any right leaning beliefs right now, and especially owning a gun, I would be very afraid of losing my job if that
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为，如果现在被贴上持有任何右翼信仰的标签，尤其是还拥有一支枪，如果这些

sentences.en: became public.
sentences.zh: 公开的话，我会非常担心失去工作。

sentences.en: And after explaining that he was nervous about possible consequences of sharing his story, he began to lay out how it is he came to be so anxious about this political moment.
sentences.zh: 在解释了他对分享自己故事可能带来的后果感到担忧后，他开始讲述自己是如何对当前的政治氛围感到如此焦虑的。

sentences.en: Can we just start at the beginning?
sentences.zh: 我们能从头说起吗？

sentences.en: Uh, where did you grow up and what was your experience like in your home, uh, around politics and specifically around guns?
sentences.zh: 呃，你在哪里长大的？在家里，呃，围绕政治特别是围绕枪支，你的经历是怎样的？

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: Uh, I grew up in, um, kind of all over the Midwest, um, but mostly rural South Dakota and rural Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 呃，我是在，嗯，中西部各地长大的，呃，不过大部分时间是在南达科他州农村和明尼苏达州农村。

sentences.en: My parents are both highly educated, you know, at least sort of very liberal for where we lived at the time.
sentences.zh: 我的父母都受过高等教育，你知道的，至少以我们当时居住的地方来看，他们思想非常自由派。

sentences.en: Um, now that I live in Seattle, I think about it a little differently, but, uh, they were always sort of the
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在我住在西雅图，对此我的看法有点不同了，但是，呃，他们一直可以说是

sentences.en: Democrats in arguments with the rest of the Republican family at Thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 感恩节聚会上与其余共和党亲属争论不休的民主党人。

sentences.en: Uh, I definitely have some memories of that.
sentences.zh: 呃，我对那确实有一些记忆。

sentences.en: He says that even though he knew lots of conservatives, he and his family were in line with the political left.
sentences.zh: 他说，尽管他认识很多保守派，但他和家人一直与政治左翼保持一致。

sentences.en: You know, gay marriage, you know, that was a very important issue for me.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，同性恋婚姻，你知道的，这对当时的我来说是一个非常重要的议题。

sentences.en: I, I still believe that sort of there should be a single payer government option healthcare.
sentences.zh: 我，我仍然认为，某种程度上应该实行单一支付方的政府医疗保障体系。

sentences.en: Like, I think that would be a good thing for this country.
sentences.zh: 比如，我认为这对这个国家是一件好事。

sentences.en: Including issues about guns.
sentences.zh: 包括关于枪支的议题。

sentences.en: My father and my mother and I, like we all believed in gun control and my dad still doesn't own a pistol.
sentences.zh: 我父亲、母亲和我，我们都信仰枪支管制，我爸至今没有手枪。

sentences.en: Uh, every gun that he owns is a hunting gun.
sentences.zh: 呃，他拥有的每一支枪都是猎枪。

sentences.en: My dad loved hunting.
sentences.zh: 我爸热爱打猎。

sentences.en: Uh, he would take me hunting and fishing as a kid.
sentences.zh: 呃，他小时候经常带我去打猎和钓鱼。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, when we thought about gun control, it's like, well, you know, why do you need, you know, why might you need a pistol?
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道的，当我们想到枪支管制时，就会觉得，好吧，你知道的，你为什么需要，你知道的，你为什么会需要一把手枪？

sentences.en: Or like, why might you need, well, the AR-15 that I own now?
sentences.zh: 或者说，为什么会需要，嗯，我现在拥有的这把AR-15？

sentences.en: Uh, definitely, you know, that would have been something that we didn't want.
sentences.zh: 呃，毫无疑问，你知道的，那绝对是我们不想要的东西。

sentences.en: Walk me through as you got older, um,
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲随着你年龄的增长，嗯，

sentences.en: first, like how you saw yourself politically as you kind of came into your own and whether or not guns played any role in that along the way.
sentences.zh: 首先，随着你逐渐走向成熟，你是如何看待自己的政治立场的，以及枪支在这个过程中是否发挥了任何作用。

sentences.en: Sure, sure.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然。

sentences.en: Um, I definitely identified politically as Democrat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的政治立场明确倾向于民主党。

sentences.en: The first time I was eligible to vote was the 2008 election and I voted for Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 我第一次有资格投票是2008年大选，我投给了巴拉克·奥巴马。

sentences.en: I definitely identified as a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 我绝对把自己当作民主党人。

sentences.en: I mean, really, honestly, until sort of this whole COVID thing came about.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的，老实说，直到整个新冠疫情爆发之前都是如此。

sentences.en: And so up to this point, he's basically been in alignment with all of the big progressive issues.
sentences.zh: 所以到目前为止，他在所有重大进步主义议题上基本都保持一致。

sentences.en: But when it came to the handling of the coronavirus...
sentences.zh: 但当谈到对新冠病毒的处理时……

sentences.en: I will say that I think the initial shutdown, there's a really good case to be made for it.
sentences.zh: 我得说，我认为最初的封城，确实有其充分的理由。

sentences.en: I don't think I would have done it, but we didn't have any masks.
sentences.zh: 我可能不会那么做，但当时我们没有任何口罩。

sentences.en: We didn't have any testing.
sentences.zh: 我们没有任何检测手段。

sentences.en: How else are you going to try to check the spread of the virus?
sentences.zh: 除此之外，你还能怎么去遏制病毒的传播？

sentences.en: I think by June, though, we had masks and we had testing.
sentences.zh: 不过我认为到了六月份，我们已经有口罩了，也有检测了。

sentences.en: And yet people were still arguing for lockdowns.
sentences.zh: 然而人们仍然在争论是否要封城。

sentences.en: And I'm like, you know, can we at least let young people go back to work?
sentences.zh: 我就想，你知道的，我们至少能让年轻人回去工作吗？

sentences.en: He just disagreed with the conventional thinking.
sentences.zh: 他只是不同意传统观念的看法。

sentences.en: And he felt that there wasn't really any place for him to give voice to that.
sentences.zh: 而且他觉得现实中并没有什么地方能让他表达这种心声。

sentences.en: When I would say things like this, or when other people would say things like this,
sentences.zh: 每当我这样说的时候，或者当其他人这样说的时候，

sentences.en: it, uh, the, the response was always like, you are not an authority that we truSt. And I would say,
sentences.zh: 这，呃，回应总是像：你并非我们信任的权威。而我会说，

sentences.en: okay, but there are other authorities, you know, who are saying the things I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 好的，但是还有其他权威，你知道的，他们也在说我所说的话。

sentences.en: And they're like, well, we don't trust them either.
sentences.zh: 而他们会说，好吧，我们也不信任他们。

sentences.en: And I'm like, okay, so, you know, is being authority really the problem?
sentences.zh: 我就想，好吧，所以，你知道的，身为权威真的是问题所在吗？

sentences.en: Or is it just not saying what you want to hear?
sentences.zh: 还是说只是因为没有说出你想听的话？

sentences.en: That's the problem.
sentences.zh: 这才是问题所在。

sentences.en: That's what it felt like.
sentences.zh: 感觉就是这样。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So as the COVID lockdowns are happening, you're finding yourself feeling like you're arguing with people who usually feel more like political allies.
sentences.zh: 所以在新冠封城期间，你发现自己感觉像是在和那些通常更像是政治盟友的人争论。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, um, you know, I have a, I have a group of really close friends and, um, the discussion last year was, is Bernie the right candidate?
sentences.zh: 我是说，嗯，你知道的，我有一群非常要好的朋友，嗯，去年的讨论是，伯尼是合适的候选人吗？

sentences.en: Are there any other candidates who are good enough for us?
sentences.zh: 还有没有其他候选人对我们来说足够好？

sentences.en: And, um, um, I'm one of two in the group.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，嗯，我是我们这群人里仅有的两个持这种想法的人之一。

sentences.en: The other who has the same training that I do.
sentences.zh: 另一个人接受过和我一样的训练。

sentences.en: We're both questioning the COVID stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都在质疑新冠相关的那些事。

sentences.en: And he says that part of all this is that as the lockdown wore on, the effect of a lockdown, this thing that he didn't even agree with in the first place, he started to feel it.
sentences.zh: 他说，这一切的一部分在于，随着封城持续下去，封城带来的影响——这件他一开始甚至并不同意的事情——他开始切身感受到了。

sentences.en: I'm a very introverted person.
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常内向的人。

sentences.en: And so honestly, for the first month or two, you know, I felt great.
sentences.zh: 所以老实说，在前一两个月，你知道的，我感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: I was like, wow, like I don't have to commute to work.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，哇，我不用通勤去上班了。

sentences.en: Like I have all this time.
sentences.zh: 我有这么多时间。

sentences.en: Um, but I think that the isolation sort of did get to me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为孤立感确实开始折磨我了。

sentences.en: Uh, it took me longer than most, but it did get to me.
sentences.zh: 呃，虽然我比大多数人适应的时间要长，但它确实影响到我了。

sentences.en: And when he started talking about this with one of his friends, I'm like, you know, it's driving me crazy and I just feel trapped.
sentences.zh: 当他开始和其中一个朋友谈起这件事时，我就说，你知道的，这快把我逼疯了，我只觉得被困住了。

sentences.en: And he said he was going through the same stuff.
sentences.zh: 而他说他也在经历同样的事情。

sentences.en: He's like, you know, I'm feeling a lot of stress.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，我感到了很大的压力。

sentences.en: He's like, but when I find myself getting caught in it, he's like, I force myself to turn it into action.
sentences.zh: 他说，但每当我发现自己陷入其中时，他说，我强迫自己把这转化为行动。

sentences.en: This friend suggested that, you know, he finds some way to take back some control of his life.
sentences.zh: 这位朋友建议，你知道的，让他找个方法重新掌控自己的一部分生活。

sentences.en: You know, and that was when I realized I'm like, oh, like I have lost my sense of individual power and recommended to him that he consider buying a firearm.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，也就是在那时我意识到，哦，我失去了对个人力量的掌控感，并建议他考虑买一支枪。

sentences.en: And so I made the decision to buy a gun.
sentences.zh: 于是我决定买一把枪。

sentences.en: And so that was the plan.
sentences.zh: 所以计划就是这样。

sentences.en: And then George Floyd died.
sentences.zh: 然后乔治·弗洛伊德死了。

sentences.en: The death of George Floyd started peacefully, but has turned very destructive tonight.
sentences.zh: 乔治·弗洛伊德之死最初是以和平方式开始的，但在今晚变得极具破坏性。

sentences.en: Then there were riots in Seattle.
sentences.zh: 接着西雅图就发生了骚乱。

sentences.en: My wife and I got a notification.

sentences.zh: 我只是觉得更震惊、更意外，因为，你知道的，他就是那个《学徒》里的老兄，还顶着滑稽的

sentences.en: hair, and said all this stupid stuff, and it just was, like, shocking that he was elected.
sentences.zh: 头发，满嘴胡言乱语，他能当选简直太让人震惊了。

sentences.en: It wasn't like, oh, I got to get a gun, because Trump was president.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说，天哪，因为特朗普当选总统了，我得去买支枪。

sentences.en: It wasn't, it wasn't like that.
sentences.zh: 不是的，根本不是那样的。

sentences.en: But then,
sentences.zh: 但后来，

sentences.en: there was Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 发生了夏洛茨维尔事件。

sentences.en: I just remember those guys with the, the torches, and, like, right by their faces, and just kind of marching in unison, and also the image of, you know, the car driving through.
sentences.zh: 我还记得那些拿着火把的家伙，火把就在他们脸旁边，迈着整齐的步伐游行，还有那辆车冲过去的画面。

sentences.en: A car barreling down the street.
sentences.zh: 一辆车猛地冲下街道。

sentences.en: That's 4th and Water Street in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 那是夏洛茨维尔的第四街和水街交叉口。

sentences.en: And there was a lot after Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 夏洛茨维尔事件之后还发生了许多事。

sentences.en: Loved ones of Breonna Taylor grieving and outraged.
sentences.zh: 布伦娜·泰勒的亲人们悲痛欲绝、愤怒不已。

sentences.en: We report again tonight on the fatal shooting of Ahmaud Arbery.
sentences.zh: 今晚我们再次报道艾马德·阿伯里遭枪杀身亡事件。

sentences.en: This case is...
sentences.zh: 这个案子是……

sentences.en: George Floyd repeatedly told the officers that he could not breathe.
sentences.zh: 乔治·弗洛伊德多次告诉警察他喘不过气来。

sentences.en: Ahmaud Arbery, Breonna Taylor, George Floyd.
sentences.zh: 艾马德·阿伯里、布伦娜·泰勒、乔治·弗洛伊德。

sentences.en: For Ashley, it wasn't just the horror of so many Black people killed at the hands of police, but also the fact that when people took to the streets to protest this injustice,
sentences.zh: 对阿什利来说，不仅是那么多黑人死于警察之手让她感到恐惧，还有当人们走上街头抗议这种不公时，

sentences.en: she saw scenes of them being met by white counter-protesters, people she associated with the right, carrying guns.
sentences.zh: 她看到他们遭遇了白人反抗议者的阻挠，那些她认为属于右翼、带着枪的人。

sentences.en: We're also learning more tonight about the 17-year-old from a neighboring state, now accused of opening fire on protesters.
sentences.zh: 今晚我们还了解到更多关于那个来自邻州、被指控向抗议者开枪的17岁少年的消息。

sentences.en: Two were killed.
sentences.zh: 两人死亡。

sentences.en: These people aren't playing around now.
sentences.zh: 这些人现在可不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: It's more than just sitting online and saying racist stuff in the comments on news articles.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是坐在网上的新闻文章评论区里发表种族主义言论。

sentences.en: These people are now showing up to places and with the intent to cause people harm.
sentences.zh: 这些人现在开始出现在现场，并怀着伤害他人的意图。

sentences.en: Even when the protests were about COVID, people protesting the lockdowns,
sentences.zh: 甚至当抗议活动是关于新冠疫情、人们抗议封锁时，

sentences.en: Ashley saw the same thing.
sentences.zh: 阿什利也看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: One day, she turned on her TV.
sentences.zh: 有一天，她打开了电视。

sentences.en: Police positioned themselves on essentially every corner around downtown Raleigh this morning just to keep the peace.
sentences.zh: 今天早上，警察基本上在罗利市中心周围的每个街角都部署了警力，只是为了维持秩序。

sentences.en: And saw a group of people
sentences.zh: 然后看到了一群人

sentences.en: A bunch of white people, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 基本上都是一群白人。

sentences.en: Walking the streets of Raleigh, the state capital, with assault rifles.
sentences.zh: 带着突击步枪在州首府罗利的街头游荡。

sentences.en: It felt like a huge threat.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是一个巨大的威胁。

sentences.en: Then finally one day, Ashley saw something she hadn't really seen before.
sentences.zh: 直到终于有一天，阿什利看到了她以前从未真正见过的东西。

sentences.en: I think the exact moment I knew I had to buy a gun was watching the NFAC, which is the Not Fucking Around Coalition, which is basically an armed black militia.
sentences.zh: 我想我决定必须买枪的准确时刻，是看到了NFAC，也就是“绝不废话联盟”（Not Fucking Around Coalition），这基本上是一个武装黑人民兵组织。

sentences.en: We here!
sentences.zh: 我们在这儿！

sentences.en: Where the fuck you at?
sentences.zh: 你们他妈的在哪儿？

sentences.en: We in your house!
sentences.zh: 我们就在你家！

sentences.en: And they were counter-protesting to the KKK and white supremacist groups who were trying to rally in
sentences.zh: 他们在抗议3K党和白人至上主义团体的集会，那些人试图在

sentences.en: Stone Mountain, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州的斯通芒特进行集会。

sentences.en: And so there were, like, thousands of black people with guns, like, marching.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有成千上万带枪的黑人在游行。

sentences.en: Threat, counter-threat.
sentences.zh: 威胁对抗威胁。

sentences.en: Cause threats don't mean shit to us.
sentences.zh: 因为威胁对我们来说屁都不是。

sentences.en: NFAC, motherfucker!
sentences.zh: NFAC，他妈的！

sentences.en: Black people aren't encouraged to openly carry or to bear arMs. And there's lots of reasons for that,
sentences.zh: 黑人并不被鼓励公开持枪或携带武器。这有很多原因，

sentences.en: and there's consequences to us for doing that that aren't there for white people.
sentences.zh: 而且我们这样做会承担白人所没有的后果。

sentences.en: And it was, it was, it was powerful to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说，真的非常有冲击力。

sentences.en: We haven't really seen black people showing up armed and not aggressively, just walking around, just like the white supremacists do,
sentences.zh: 我们以前没见过黑人武装出现，而且不是带着攻击性，只是四处走动，就像白人至上主义者那样，

sentences.en: just like you have a right in this country to do.
sentences.zh: 就像你在这个国家有权做的那样。

sentences.en: So finally, after months, Ashley goes online and buys a weapon.
sentences.zh: 于是终于在几个月后，阿什利上网买了一把武器。

sentences.en: Can you show me your gun?
sentences.zh: 你能给我看看你的枪吗？

sentences.en: Uh, so it's a Canic 9mm that holds 14 rounds.
sentences.zh: 呃，这是一把能装14发子弹的Canik 9毫米手枪。

sentences.en: Honestly, I just wanted to get it fast, as I could, because I was starting to get nervous that it would be harder to get or a longer period to wait.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我只是想尽快买到手，因为我开始担心以后会更难买到，或者要等待更长时间。

sentences.en: And so I just bought one to have one with the intention of, you know, going and practicing more with different kinds to find one that I really, really become one with it, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以我买一把先备着，打算是以后去多用不同型号的枪练习，找到一把真正能与我融为一体的枪，你懂的。

sentences.en: In fact, the guns still feel so alien to Ashley that she practices just holding it in her hands at least twice a week.
sentences.zh: 事实上，枪对阿什利来说仍然感到很陌生，以至于她每周至少练习两次把它拿在手里。

sentences.en: Sit on the bed and kind of hold it and, you know, take the clip out and, you know, just stand up and put it
sentences.zh: 坐在床上拿着它，把弹夹卸下来，然后站起来，

sentences.en: from hand to hand and look through the sights.
sentences.zh: 从一只手换到另一只手，透过瞄准具看。

sentences.en: But Ashley isn't just getting comfortable with the physical feel of the gun.
sentences.zh: 但阿什利不仅是在适应枪支的实体手感。

sentences.en: I was once the type of person who would think, like, I could never shoot somebody, I could never do anything to defend myself in that type of way,
sentences.zh: 我曾经是那种会认为“我绝不可能开枪打人，我绝不可能用这种方式保护自己”的人，

sentences.en: because I just was never, I never felt like that type of person.
sentences.zh: 因为我从来不是、也从不觉得自己是那种人。

sentences.en: But, like, the older that I'm getting, like, I don't really feel that way.
sentences.zh: 但是，随着年龄越来越大，我不再那样觉得了。

sentences.en: Like, if it's me or somebody, like, it is going to be me.
sentences.zh: 如果不是我死，就是别人死，那只能是我活下来。

sentences.en: Wait, what do you mean when you say that?
sentences.zh: 等等，你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: If I feel threatened, then I want to feel empowered to defend myself.
sentences.zh: 如果我感到受到威胁，那么我想拥有自卫的力量。

sentences.en: And I've made myself okay with what that may mean.
sentences.zh: 我已经说服自己接受这意味着什么。

sentences.en: It definitely wasn't an easy decision.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是一个容易的决定。

sentences.en: But that's kind of where I am with it.
sentences.zh: 但这差不多就是我现在的态度。

sentences.en: You have repeatedly criticized the vice president for not specifically calling out Antifa.
sentences.zh: 你一再批评副总统没有明确点名谴责安提法（Antifa）。

sentences.en: I spoke to Ashley shortly after the first presidential debate.
sentences.zh: 我在第一场总统辩论结束不久后采访了阿什利。

sentences.en: To condemn white supremacists and militia groups.
sentences.zh: 去谴责白人至上主义者和民兵团。队。

sentences.en: And it was clear that watching the debate had only given Ashley more reason to believe that her fears of what might happen might actually be realized.
sentences.zh: 很明显，观看这场辩论让阿什利更加确信，她对可能发生的事情的恐惧或许真的会变成现实。

sentences.en: What are you saying?
sentences.zh: 你在说什么？

sentences.en: I'm willing to do anything.
sentences.zh: 我愿意做任何事。

sentences.en: I want to see peace.
sentences.zh: 我想看到和平。

sentences.en: Then do it, sir.
sentences.zh: 那就做啊，先生。

sentences.en: Say it.
sentences.zh: 说出来。

sentences.en: Do it.
sentences.zh: 做啊。

sentences.en: Say it.
sentences.zh: 说出来。

sentences.en: You know, they asked him about the Proud Boys, and he said to tell the Proud Boys,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们问到关于“骄傲男孩”的事，而他说要告诉“骄傲男孩”，

sentences.en: Proud Boys, stand back and stand by.
sentences.zh: “骄傲男孩”，退后并随时待命。

sentences.en: And then a few minutes later, he mentioned something about his supporters going to the polls.
sentences.zh: 然后几分钟后，他提到了关于他的支持者去投票站的事。

sentences.en: Will you urge your supporters to stay calm, not to engage in any civil unrest?
sentences.zh: 你会敦促你的支持者保持冷静，不要参与任何内乱吗？

sentences.en: President Trump, you go firSt.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统，您先请。

sentences.en: I'm urging my supporters to go into the polls and watch very carefully, because that's what has to happen.
sentences.zh: 我正敦促我的支持者进入投票站并仔细监视，因为这就是必须发生的事情。

sentences.en: I am urging them to do it.
sentences.zh: 我正在敦促他们这么做。

sentences.en: All that is just encouraging people to be intimidating.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都只是在鼓励人们搞恐吓。

sentences.en: If I see tens of thousands of ballots being manipulated, I can't go along with that.
sentences.zh: 如果我看到几万张选票被操纵，我是无法接受的。

sentences.en: And I'll tell you what, from a common sense, I'll tell you what it means.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你吧，从常识角度来说，我告诉你这意味着什么。

sentences.en: It means you have a fraudulent election.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这是一场充满欺诈的选举。

sentences.en: Like, he used that entire debate to illegitimize the election so that if he does not win, he can rally up his supporters to respond to that.
sentences.zh: 他是利用整场辩论来使选举失去合法性，这样如果他输了，他就可以号召支持者来做出回应。

sentences.en: That is scary, because like I said, they know how to get guns.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了，因为就像我说的，他们知道怎么弄到枪。

sentences.en: They have access to them.
sentences.zh: 他们能搞到枪。

sentences.en: They have them stockpiled.
sentences.zh: 他们囤积了枪支。

sentences.en: Like, these are people that have been preparing their whole lives for something to pop off, and they're just waiting for the word.
sentences.zh: 这些人一生都在为爆发冲突做准备，他们只是在等一声令下。

sentences.en: And he's telling them in so many words, I'm going to give you the word.
sentences.zh: 而他等于是明明白白地告诉他们，我会给你们下达指令。

sentences.en: And if I don't win this election, you know what to do.
sentences.zh: 如果我赢得不了这次选举，你们知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: Do you think that the other side is as afraid of you as you are of them?
sentences.zh: 你觉得对方害怕你们，就像你们害怕他们一样吗？

sentences.en: I don't think the other side.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得对方……

sentences.en: I think the other side has been kind of conditioned to be afraid of us their whole lives.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对方一生中都被灌输了害怕我们的观念。

sentences.en: So, yeah, yeah, I'm sure they are scared, but it's not even us.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，是的，我确信他们很害怕，但这甚至都不是因为我们。

sentences.en: It's like a, it's like a figment of their, their mind.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，这就像是他们脑海中的一个虚构幻象。

sentences.en: Right before dinner, Ashley and Nikki sat in the living room comparing guns.
sentences.zh: 晚饭前，阿什利和妮基坐在客厅里对比着各自的枪。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: See, is it hard on your thumbs?
sentences.zh: 看，按这个弹夹费劲吗？

sentences.en: Pop that clip out.
sentences.zh: 把那个弹夹退出来。

sentences.en: No, yours isn't bad at all.
sentences.zh: 不，你的这一点都不费劲。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Terrica, what are you shooting, love?
sentences.zh: 特里卡，宝贝，你带了什么枪？

sentences.en: Excuse me, she's got a real arm.
sentences.zh: 不好意思，她可是个大力士。

sentences.en: I'll shoot it, um, okay.
sentences.zh: 我要开枪，嗯，好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, but hopefully it's a 45.
sentences.zh: 我是说，但愿是把45口径的。

sentences.en: I mean, anything else I'm scared, I might cry again.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，换别的任何枪我都害怕，我可能会再次哭出来。

sentences.en: Terrica, Ashley's girlfriend, was worried about the morning.
sentences.zh: 特里卡，阿什利的女朋友，正为早上的事感到担忧。

sentences.en: She and Ashley had actually gone to a shooting range a few months back when they first started thinking about this, and it hadn't gone well.
sentences.zh: 她和阿什利其实在几个月前刚开始产生这个想法时去过一次射击场，结果不太顺利。

sentences.en: I thought this would be all cute, like, you know, like Charlie Angels.
sentences.zh: 我以为这会很酷炫，就像，你知道的，像《查理的天使》那样。

sentences.en: And just like, you know, I was practicing my poses, like, you know, the whole ice cream thing from Friday.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，我一直在练习摆姿势，就像，你知道的，周五里吃冰淇淋的那种经典架势。

sentences.en: But then, you know, when I shot it, it just got really real, really quick.
sentences.zh: 但然后，你知道的，当我开枪时，情况立刻变得非常真实。

sentences.en: Terrica says, as soon as the gun kicked back.
sentences.zh: 特里卡说，就在后坐力把枪震开的那一刻。

sentences.en: Ashley, did I cry like a baby?
sentences.zh: 阿什利，我当时哭得像个婴儿吗？

sentences.en: She started bawling uncontrollably.
sentences.zh: 她开始不可遏制地放声大哭。

sentences.en: Ugly cry, like, I almost dropped the gun and a woman on safety cry.
sentences.zh: 丑陋的大哭，就像，我差点把枪扔了，那种安全员看了都想哭的程度。

sentences.en: And I just was shaking, my whole body was shaking from the top to the bottom.
sentences.zh: 我一直在发抖，从头到脚浑身都在抖。

sentences.en: But even though the first time was a little bit traumatizing, Terrica was going to give it another go in the morning.
sentences.zh: 但尽管第一次有点创伤性，特里卡还是决定明天早上再去试一次。

sentences.en: Is there something specific that you're worried about?
sentences.zh: 你有什么特别担心的吗？

sentences.en: I'm definitely worried about the election.
sentences.zh: 我绝对担心选举。

sentences.en: I'm worried about being black.
sentences.zh: 我担心身为黑人这件事。

sentences.en: Like, I don't want to be a sitting duck.
sentences.zh: 就像，我可不想当任人宰割的活靶子。

sentences.en: Before I left for the night, the three women gathered together in the living room for a toaSt.
sentences.zh: 在我离开过夜前，三位女性聚在客厅里举杯庆祝。

sentences.en: What do we toast?
sentences.zh: 我们为庆祝什么干杯？

sentences.en: Cheers to guns.
sentences.zh: 为枪支干杯。

sentences.en: We're all being very brave going to take this class tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天去上这门课，都非常勇敢。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In the morning, we all meet at an outdoor range.
sentences.zh: 早上，我们在一个户外射击场集合。

sentences.en: The class is Ashley, Terrica, Nikki, and five other women.
sentences.zh: 上课的有阿什利、特里卡、妮基和其他五位女性。

sentences.en: The training is run by this organization called Girls on Fire, which specifically trains women of color and apparently has a waiting list of 80 people.
sentences.zh: 这次培训由一个叫“烈火女孩”（Girls on Fire）的组织举办，专门培训有色人种女性，据说候补名单上已经有80人了。

sentences.en: All the women mill and chat as the trainer and her assistant get things organized.
sentences.zh: 当教练和助手整理东西时，所有女性都在四处走动闲聊。

sentences.en: They lay out guns on the table while explaining there's now a massive shortage of bullets.
sentences.zh: 她们把枪摆在桌上，同时解释说现在子弹严重短缺。

sentences.en: Ammo is really hard to find.
sentences.zh: 弹药真的很难找。

sentences.en: Yeah, I tried to get some yesterday.
sentences.zh: 对，我昨天尝试买一些。

sentences.en: They only had holidays.
sentences.zh: 他们只有节假日特供。

sentences.en: You know, even us with having a class, we almost had to cancel because it was so hard to find an ammo to use.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，连我们办培训班都差点取消，因为实在太难找到可以用的弹药了。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful day and the sun is out and Ashley seems fine.
sentences.zh: 今天天气晴朗，阳光明媚，阿什利看起来状态不错。

sentences.en: But before the training really gets started, I notice her girlfriend, Terrica, is visibly jumping every time a gun goes off.
sentences.zh: 但在培训正式开始前，我注意到她的女友特里卡每当听到枪声就会明显地吓得跳起来。

sentences.en: She seems terrified.
sentences.zh: 她看起来吓坏了。

sentences.en: And after a few minutes, she breaks away from the group to go to the car and Ashley follows her.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，她脱离了队伍走向汽车，阿什利也跟了上去。

sentences.en: It's just making her nervous, but she'll be all right.
sentences.zh: 这只是让她有点紧张，但她会没事的。

sentences.en: She just got to calm down.
sentences.zh: 她只是得冷静下来。

sentences.en: Terrica sits in the car trying to steady herself.
sentences.zh: 特里卡坐在车里试图让自己平静下来。

sentences.en: And eventually gets out and makes her way to the table where the guns are laid out.
sentences.zh: 最终她下了车，走向摆放着枪支的桌子。

sentences.en: How you doing?
sentences.zh: 你感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm scared from the noise, but I can do it.
sentences.zh: 这噪音让我害怕，但我能做到。

sentences.en: I can do this shit.

sentences.en: I served in the United States Army.

sentences.en: On one of my last days of reporting, this thing happened while I was standing in line talking to people in front of one of these gun shops.
sentences.zh: 在我最后几天的采访中，发生了一件事，当时我正站在这些枪店外排队和人们聊天。

sentences.en: I'm tired of you.

sentences.en: I'm not a second-rate citizen.
sentences.zh: 我不是二等公民。

sentences.en: I'm a citizen.
sentences.zh: 我是个公民。

sentences.en: I was talking to this guy in line who was wearing a Black Lives Matter hoodie.
sentences.zh: 我当时正在和排在我前面一个穿着“黑人的命也是命”连帽衫的家伙聊天。

sentences.en: I encourage every brother who can legally carry it, get a motherfucking gun.
sentences.zh: 我鼓励每一个有合法持枪资格的兄弟，去他妈的搞支枪。

sentences.en: Get as many guns as you can afford, you know, because you know what?

sentences.en: The police are here to protect and serve, not to harass and abuse.
sentences.zh: 警察是来保护和服务的，而不是来骚扰和虐待的。

sentences.en: You probably ain't never been fucked up by the police.

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.zh: 整个队伍都安静了下来。

sentences.zh: 所有这些紧张气氛都被加剧了，因为这两个家伙，实际上这队里的大多数人都带着枪。

sentences.en: Do you have something you want to say?

sentences.zh: 我说过了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Eventually, I walked over and I asked the guy if he had anything else that he wanted to say.
sentences.zh: 最终，我走过去问那个人他还有没有什么想说的。

sentences.en: The movement, the movement is bogus.
sentences.zh: 这场运动，这场运动是个骗局。

sentences.en: He said that Black Lives Matter was bogus, but then he waved me away, didn't want to talk to me anymore.
sentences.zh: 他说“黑人的命也是命”是个骗局，但随后他挥手把我打发走，不想再跟我说话了。

sentences.en: So eventually, I just went back over to talk again with the man in the BLM hoodie.
sentences.zh: 所以最后，我又回去和穿BLM连帽衫的那个人聊天。

sentences.en: Yeah, your message is, now is a good time to get a firearm.

sentences.zh: 那是一种权利。

sentences.en: Your driving license is a privilege.

sentences.en: This is a right.

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?

sentences.en: Everyone in this line was still quiet.
sentences.zh: 队伍里的每个人都依然安静。

sentences.zh: 就像，他们只是站在那里看着我们，然后又看着那个剃光头的男人。

sentences.en: I just want to make sure we don't escalate tensions too much with this gentleman, but I also don't want you to be robbed of your point of view.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确保我们不会跟这位先生把紧张局势升级得太厉害，但我也希望你不会被剥夺表达观点的权力。

sentences.en: Yeah, but no.
sentences.zh: 对，但是算了。

sentences.en: And then, that guy, who was just so angry seconds ago, he walked up to us.
sentences.zh: 然后，那个几秒钟前还怒气冲冲的家伙，向我们走了过来。

sentences.en: Everybody, this America, everybody got their opinion.
sentences.zh: 各位，这里是美国，每个人都有自己的观点。

sentences.en: If you feel a certain way, you know, that's how you feel.

sentences.en: You know what I mean?

sentences.en: I appreciate that.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I get hot-tempered sometimes.

sentences.en: It wasn't, I didn't even hear what he was saying to you.

sentences.zh: 我们不需要这种垃圾，这种争执。

sentences.en: We need to talk if there's any probleMs.
sentences.zh: 如果有任何问题，我们需要谈谈。

sentences.en: And then the two of these men shook hands.
sentences.zh: 然后这两个男人握了手。

sentences.en: You know how much tension this world was under?

sentences.en: But now we're talking.

sentences.en: See, because that's a, we're humans.

sentences.en: We're civilized.
